articles.title: Furacão com ventos de até 185 km/h preocupa autoridades no México | G1
articles.standfirst: Tempestade deve trazer muita chuva, aumentando o risco de inundações e deslizamentos de terra que podem causar mortes, informou Centro Nacional de Furacões dos EUA.
articles.summary: Tempestade deve trazer muita chuva, aumentando o risco de inundações e deslizamentos de terra que podem causar mortes, informou Centro Nacional de Furacões dos EUA.
articles.body:
A costa oeste do México se prepara para a chegada do furacão Polo, previsto para tocar o solo de Baja California Sur, estado banhado pelo Oceano Pacífico, nesta segunda-feira (28). O fenômeno deve tocar o solo às 19h no horário de Brasília, que é quando os maiores danos devem acontecer.

Os primeiros efeito já começaram a ser sentidos. Em Puerto San Carlos, na Baixa Califórnia Sul, já há registro de fortes ventos, elevação do nível do mar e alagamentos. A água já rompeu trechos de uma barreira de areia que protegia o vilarejo e começou a invadir as ruas. O fornecimento de energia elétrica também foi interrompido.

As palmeiras se curvam com a força do vento, enquanto moradores deixam suas casas e procuram abrigos.

As autoridades mexicanas emitiram um alerta aos moradores da região advertindo sobre os ventos fortes e a possibilidade de enchentes repentinas que podem causar mortes.

"Antes que o furacão Polo atinja a costa, desligue os aparelhos elétricos e tenha uma fonte de luz alternativa à mão", disse o escritório de proteção civil em uma publicação na rede social X, acrescentando que pode haver cortes de energia.

Na manhã desta segunda, o furacão de categoria 3 estava a cerca de 175 km a sudoeste de Cabo San Lázaro, com ventos máximos sustentados próximos a 185 km/h e rajadas ainda mais fortes, de acordo com o Centro Nacional de Furacões dos EUA (NHC).

Segundo o órgão americano, o Polo deve causar uma precipitação de até 300 milímetros de chuva , o que indica um grande risco de inundações e deslizamentos de terra que podem causar mortes.

Funcionário de restaurante em Loreto, no México, protege fachada do local com fita e tapumes para a chegada do furacão Polo — Foto: REUTERS/Raquel Cunha

Após passar pela península da Baja California, lar de destinos turísticos como Los Cabos e o Arco de Cabo San Lucas, espera-se que a tempestade perca força.

Nos últimos dias, ela já causou fortes chuvas, ondas destrutivas e ventos intensos, provocando evacuações, fechamento de portos e cancelamento de aulas no território mexicano.

Duas crianças morreram e seus pais continuam desaparecidos depois que sua casa foi arrastada pela correnteza no estado de Jalisco, enquanto uma jovem foi levada por fortes correntes nas praias de Puerto Vallarta, de acordo com as autoridades locais.

A Guarda Nacional já percorre as ruas orientando a população a se proteger. Moradores reforçaram portas e janelas com tábuas e sacos de areia.

Em Puerto San Carlos, que tem cerca de 6.000 habitantes, está entre as áreas mais afetadas pela passagem de ciclones. As autoridades disponibilizaram 169 abrigos no estado e determinaram a suspensão de aulas, atividades marítimas e acesso às praias.

"Este vai ser muito pior, vai causar mais estragos", afirmou à AFP María Palomino, de 57 anos, moradora da cidade.

O mar é uma das principais preocupações. A barreira de areia que servia de contenção já foi ultrapassada pela água em alguns pontos.

Um policial que passava pelo local avaliou que o povoado deveria ter sido evacuado. "A escola vai inundar, tudo vai inundar", disse.

As Forças Armadas mobilizaram quase 7.000 militares na Baixa Califórnia Sul para atuar durante a passagem do furacão.

Moradores também adotaram medidas de prevenção antes da chegada de Polo. Casas e estabelecimentos comerciais foram protegidos com tábuas e sacos de areia, enquanto parte da população buscou abrigo na casa de familiares ou nas estruturas montadas pelas autoridades.

Polo é o primeiro furacão da temporada a tocar terra na região. A previsão é de que o ciclone provoque chuvas intensas, inundações e novos cortes de energia durante a passagem pelo estado.

articles.title: Debate ao governo do CE: Vera e Huggo se enfrentam sem Ciro e Elmano | G1
articles.standfirst: Os candidatos do PT e PSDB desistiram da participação ainda nesta segunda. Vera Lúcia foi convidada e Delegado Huggo conseguiu a participação por meio de uma decisão judicial.
articles.summary: Os candidatos do PT e PSDB desistiram da participação ainda nesta segunda. Vera Lúcia foi convidada e Delegado Huggo conseguiu a participação por meio de uma decisão judicial.
articles.body:
Delegado Huggo (Missão) e Vera Lúcia (Novo) participam de debate da TV Cidade. — Foto: Reprodução/ Youtube.

Os candidatos Delegado Huggo (Missão) e Vera Lúcia (Novo) participaram de debate ao governo do Ceará, nesta segunda-feira (28), em Fortaleza . O momento foi marcado também pela ausência de Ciro Gomes (PSDB) e Elmano de Freitas (PT), que estão em empate técnico na liderança da disputa , segundo a última pesquisa Quaest. Eles desistiram da participação no debate já nesta segunda.

O debate foi promovido pelo Grupo Cidade de Comunicação. Vera Lúcia foi convidada pela organização do debate; e Delegado Huggo conseguiu a participação por meio de uma decisão judicial. O confronto foi mediado pela jornalista Bianca Saraiva.

Nas redes sociais, Ciro Gomes justificou a ausência por supostas mudanças de regras no debate. "O acordo assinado em agosto entre as assessorias foi desfeito pela TV Cidade e novas regras foram criadas sem o consentimento de todos", afirmou.

Já Elmano de Freitas lamentou a ausência de Ciro, a qual chamou de "fuga", para justificar que também não iria ao debate. "Seria mais uma oportunidade de debater com ele sobre os dois lados desta eleição e quem tem projeto para o Ceará. Diante disso, deixarei o espaço para a candidata Vera Lúcia apresentar suas propostas. Espero que Ciro não fuja amanhã", disse.

A dinâmica do debate deixou os candidatos livres para escolher os temas a serem conversados. Com isso, duas temáticas se sobressaíram: o combate à corrupção e às facções criminosas — ambos levantados em meio a críticas ao governo atual, gestão de Elmano de Freitas.

O debate foi dividido em quatro blocos: nos três primeiros, os candidatos faziam perguntas de tema livre com até 1 min para a pergunta; o concorrente tinha 2 min para a resposta. Em seguida, quem perguntou tinha 1m45 de réplica; e, por fim, a tréplica era de até 1 min.

Confira abaixo como foi cada bloco do debate entre os candidatos:

No primeiro bloco, os candidatos fizeram perguntas de temas livres entre si. Cada candidato tinha 1 minuto para fazer uma pergunta, 2 minutos para a resposta, 1m45 para réplica e 1 minuto para a tréplica.

Vera Lúcia perguntou Delegado Huggo sobre enfrentamento às facções criminosas. O candidato do Missão aproveitou o momento para criticar a ausência de Ciro e Elmano.

“Nós vamos resolver o problema das facções criminosas com coragem. Nós vamos prender e matar todos os faccionados do estado do Ceará. Simples, efetivo. Nós vamos arrancar os faccionados de dentro da comunidade adotando a lei antifacção que foi recentemente aprovada pelo Congresso Nacional”, respondeu Delegado Huggo.

Delegado Huggo perguntou à Vera Lúcia sobre propostas na esfera fiscal e administrativa para reduzir os custos do Estado.

“O senhor já respondeu na sua própria pergunta. O Estado gasta mais do que arrecada. O estado não tem responsabilidade com o dinheiro público. É muito fácil gastar o direito dos outros. Nós precisamos de um Estado mais enxuto. Ele é responsável por saúde, educação e segurança”, respondeu a candidata do Novo.

Encerrando o bloco, Vera Lúcia perguntou ao Delegado Huggo sobre saúde pública.

“Hoje o problema de saúde é problema de gestão. Um problema de desvio de verba pública através de uma máfia de cooperativas de saúde que, inclusive, muitas delas já foram denunciadas e o governador Elmano de Freitas já foi intimado a cancelar muitos desses contratos, porque esses contratos são fraudulentos”, respondeu o candidato do Missão.

O segundo bloco teve uma dinâmica similar à do primeiro. Os candidatos fizeram perguntas de temas livres entre si. Cada candidato tinha 1 minuto para fazer uma pergunta, 2 min para a resposta, 1m45 para réplica e 1 min para a tréplica.

Delegado Huggo começou perguntando a Vera Lúcia sobre combate à corrupção.

“Na verdade, a corrupção está realmente alastrada em todas as partes do Governo, da Presidencia da República. Infelizmente é uma das coisas mais terríveis da nossa sociedade, porque ela tira o pão da boca das crianças, destrói com a força de trabalho do povo. O Partido Novo não tem ninguém envolvido em nenhum escândalo”, respondeu Vera.

Vera Lúcia perguntou sobre educação pública e citou um suposto esquema de corrupção milionário no estado.

“O que a candidata Vera está falando é só mais um exemplo de todo o modelo de corrupção e desvio de verba pública por aquele covarde ali [apontando para o púlpito vazio do candidato petista], chamado Elmano de Freitas. Ele sistematizou no estado do Ceará a corrupção entre os prefeitos através do Bebeto do Choró. O Bebeto do Choró que não é preso porque se for preso metade do PT cai junto”, respondeu Huggo.

Delegado Huggo perguntou a Vera Lúcia sobre equipamentos para cultura e esporte que são subutilizados.

“Geralmente esses gestores que estão há anos dominando o nosso estado, eles gostam muito de construção. Eles constroem mas não sabem de onde vão tirar o recurso para manter aqueles equipamentos. Não basta só construir, precisa manter esses equipamentos. Então, a harmonia entre o público e o privado é importantíssima”, respondeu Vera.

O terceiro bloco teve a mesma dinâmica dos blocos anteriores. Os candidatos fizeram perguntas de temas livres entre si. Cada candidato tinha 1 minuto para fazer uma pergunta, 2 minutos para a resposta, 1m45 para réplica e 1 minuto para a tréplica.

Delegado Huggo começou perguntando e escolheu falar de segurança pública, com foco nas facções criminosas.

“Isso é um câncer no nosso estado, no nosso país na verdade. Graças a Deus, nós do partido Novo temos o melhor projeto elaborado pelo nosso General Theophilo de segurança, que foi nosso melhor representante no governo do Bolsonaro. Mas esse projeto não é imediatista, porque nada se consegue resolver e realmente exterminar se a gente começa sendo só imediatista”, respondeu a candidata do Novo.

Vera Lúcia perguntou sobre o desaparecimento de crianças no Ceará dentro do contexto de crimes sexuais.

“Quando eu fui delegado de Quixeramobim, nós fizemos o maior enfrentamento aos crimes contra criança e adolescente; principalmente crimes de desaparecimento, de violência sexual, crimes de maus-tratos. Fizemos um enfrentamento ferrenho na cidade colocando muita gente maldosa, malvada, muitas vezes da própria família dessas crianças, na cadeia. Do mesmo modo fizemos isso em Caucaia quando eu fui delegado”, respondeu o candidato do Missão.

Encerrando o debate, no quarto bloco os candidatos tiveram 2 min para as considerações finais.

“Cearenses, eu quero terminar esse debate contando a minha história, porque ela é a história de todos vocês também. Eu não nasci de berço de ouro, eu não recebi herança política, eu não tive padrinhos que me indicaram o caminho. Tudo o que eu construí, eu construí com trabalho, com coragem, fé em quem acredita num Ceará e um Ceará que pode ser melhor. É por isso que hoje eu estou aqui. Eu não estou aqui para ser mais uma nesse confronto e nesse palanque. Eu estou aqui para ser a primeira mulher do Partido Novo no Ceará a colocar o seu nome à disposição do governo do Estado. Eu sou hoje a única mulher nordestina, pelo nosso partido, a pleitear um cargo ao governo do Estado. Eu carrego essa responsabilidade com orgulho, mas eu carrego principalmente com compromisso de governar para todos. Porque eu sei as dores das mulheres, eu sei que deve ser olhar para o filho e querer um futuro melhor e não encontrar nos nossos gestores. Eu sei o que é trabalhar, acordar cedo e não poder confiar no amanhã. Eu sei a dificuldade de uma mãe, de um pai, quando chega o final do mês. Segurança, a gente nem fala porque a gente não tem. Um filho para voltar para casa tem as dificuldades. Saúde, a gente também nem pode falar. Por isso, eu acredito que o Ceará não precisa mais de promessas. O Ceará precisa de coragem e de trabalho. Gostaria muito de agradecer a essa oportunidade, porque nós precisamos gerar mais emprego e renda para a população. Eu agradeço a Deus e a todos vocês e a esse brilhante debate e a TV Cidade por essa oportunidade. Que Deus abençoe a todos. Meu número é 30. Nós temos o melhor general e o melhor candidato ao governo, ao Senado, no Ceará”, declarou a candidata do Novo.

“Primeiramente, eu queria mandar aqui um feliz aniversário para a minha esposa, Marcela Rodrigues. Meu amor, parabéns. Que Deus te abençoe. Eu sou o homem mais feliz do mundo e mais honrado por estar ao seu lado. Muito obrigado por fazer eu ser esse homem que eu sou. Sem você, eu não seria metade disso que eu sou. Fora isso, eu queria te falar um negócio, cearense. Está na hora. Basta. Não dá mais. Não dá mais. Eu não preciso estar aqui. Eu não precisava estar aqui. Eu não preciso da política. Da onde eu vim, da onde eu nasci e cresci, eu vivo melhor do que a maior parte da população brasileira. Da minha realidade, de onde eu nasci, lá no morro, eu estou muito bem, obrigado. Eu vim para cá porque já chega. Eu não aguento mais. E eu sei que você também não aguenta. Não aguenta mais as facções. Não aguenta mais os serviços de saúde. Não aguenta mais essa educação que nós temos hoje no Estado do Ceará. Não aguenta mais a falta de emprego e renda. Não aguenta mais a falta de oportunidade para ser alguém. Você não precisa trilhar o caminho que eu trilhei, que foi muito difícil para eu estar aqui. Eu quero te ajudar a trilhar um caminho fácil. Eu quero te ajudar a conseguir ter oportunidade de emprego e renda e não depender de auxílio de governo. Não depender de Bolsa Família, não depender de Pé-de-Meia. Eu preciso que você faça um ato de revolta agora. Eu preciso que você, no dia 4 de outubro, vote 14 para o presidente Renan Santos. Para ‘desfavelizar’ o Brasil. Porque a favela vence quando ela deixa de existir. Quando ela tem serviços básicos e quando a população não é tratada como bicho, como hoje acontece. Eu preciso que você vote 14 para o governo do Estado para eu te mostrar como é possível livrar o Ceará das facções. Eu preciso que você vote 14 para deputado federal. Nós temos inúmeros deputados federais do interior. Nenhum deles é cacique político. Gente do povo para trabalhar por você. Então, no dia 4 de outubro, vote 14”, declarou o candidato do Missão.

articles.title: Gincana Consciência Limpa: Porto Velho inicia coleta de recicláveis | G1
articles.standfirst: Iniciativa da Fundação Rede Amazônica começou nesta segunda-feira (28) e mobiliza estudantes de três escolas municipais em uma disputa pela arrecadação de materiais
articles.summary: Gincana Consciência Limpa mobiliza alunos de Porto Velho na arrecadação de recicláveis para promover a educação ambiental e sustentabilidade.
articles.body:
Os primeiros materiais recicláveis começaram a chegar, nesta segunda-feira (28), às escolas participantes da Gincana Consciência Limpa, em Porto Velho . Logo no primeiro dia, estudantes levaram de casa sacolas com materiais separados para os pontos de coleta, dando início à mobilização promovida pela Fundação Rede Amazônica (FRAM).

A iniciativa reúne alunos de três escolas municipais de diferentes regiões da capital: a EMEIEF Rio Madeira, na Zona Urbana; a EMEF Estela de Araújo Compasso, na Zona Leste; e a EMEIEF Areal da Floresta, também na região urbana de Porto Velho.

Durante a gincana, os estudantes são incentivados a separar materiais recicláveis em casa e levá-los para as escolas. A proposta é transformar a coleta em uma experiência prática de educação ambiental, mostrando que atitudes simples podem fazer parte da rotina e contribuir para o descarte correto de resíduos.

Nas primeiras horas da mobilização, os alunos já chegaram às unidades de ensino carregando sacolas com materiais para a coleta. O movimento também envolve professores e equipes das escolas na organização e no acompanhamento da arrecadação.

“É um projeto que traz a consciência sobre a questão sustentável, sobre o meio ambiente, e nada melhor do que ser dentro de uma escola. Os nossos alunos são os multiplicadores, que levam toda essa consciência para dentro de casa. Eles vão fazer todo esse trabalho de arrecadação, para reciclar, mas acabam envolvendo toda a comunidade também aqui no bairro”, afirmou Érika Navarro, diretora da EMEIEF Rio Madeira.

Sacolas cheias de recicláveis marcam início da Gincana Consciência Limpa em Porto Velho — Foto: Divulgação/Rede Amazônica

Para Dênis Carvalho, especialista em Projetos da Fundação Rede Amazônica, o envolvimento dos estudantes ajuda a aproximar a educação ambiental do cotidiano.

“A participação dos alunos mostra que a educação ambiental pode começar com atitudes simples. Quando eles levam os materiais para a escola e participam da coleta, passam a entender, na prática, a importância de separar os resíduos e dar a eles a destinação correta.”

Os materiais arrecadados serão encaminhados posteriormente para destinação adequada, em parceria com cooperativas de reciclagem de Porto Velho. A iniciativa também busca estimular a responsabilidade coletiva e o trabalho em equipe entre os participantes.

A gincana segue até 9 de outubro. Ao final, os três alunos que mais se destacarem na arrecadação receberão um tablet cada. A turma com melhor desempenho coletivo será reconhecida com o título de “Turma Consciência Limpa”.

O Consciência Limpa é um projeto de educação ambiental, sustentabilidade e cidadania realizado pela Fundação Rede Amazônica (FRAM), com ações voltadas à conscientização sobre o descarte correto de resíduos, à adoção de práticas sustentáveis e à responsabilidade coletiva. Em Porto Velho, a iniciativa conta com apoio da Cidade de Porto Velho e da Rioterra.

articles.summary: Medida anunciada pelo prefeito José Ronaldo (União Brasil), nesta segunda-feira (28), beneficia 834 comerciantes de Feira de Santana. Dívida estimada é de R$ 9,6 milhões.
articles.body:
Comerciantes do Shopping Popular não pagarão aluguel dos boxes até 2028 — Foto: Fotos: Silvio Tito

Os 834 comerciantes do Shopping Popular Cidade das Compras, em Feira de Santana , seguda maior cidade da Bahia, não precisarão pagar aluguel dos boxes até dezembro de 2028. A medida foi anunciada nesta segunda-feira (28) pelo prefeito José Ronaldo de Carvalho (União Brasil), durante a assinatura da lei que autoriza a isenção.

A proposta, de autoria do Executivo Municipal, foi aprovada por unanimidade pela Câmara de Vereadores. Segundo a prefeitura, o valor da dívida assumida pelo município é estimado em R$ 9,6 milhões durante o período de vigência da medida.

O prefeito também anunciou ações para tentar revitalizar o centro comercial e atrair consumidores. Entre elas está a instalação de uma unidade da empresa de telemarketing no local, prevista para ocorrer entre fevereiro e março de 2027. A expectativa é de que 500 funcionários trabalhem no espaço.

Outra medida anunciada é a instalação da Casa do Trabalhador em uma área de 700 metros quadrados dentro do Shopping Popular.

A prefeitura também informou que será realizada uma campanha publicitária em televisão para divulgar o Shopping Popular. A propaganda está prevista para ser veiculada entre 15 de novembro e o fim de dezembro deste ano.

A secretária do Trabalho, Turismo e Desenvolvimento Econômico (Settdec), Márcia Cristina Ferreira, afirmou que as ações têm como objetivo fortalecer as vendas e melhorar as condições de trabalho dos comerciantes.

articles.standfirst: Candidata da Unidade Popular citou a operação no Complexo da Maré nesta segunda-feira (28).
articles.summary: Candidata da Unidade Popular citou a operação no Complexo da Maré nesta segunda-feira (28).
articles.body:
Juliete Pantoja (UP) conversa com eleitora em Bonsucesso, Zona Norte do Rio — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A candidata Juliete Pantoja (UP) afirmou nesta segunda-feira (28) que operações de inteligência podem ser mais eficazes no combate ao crime organizado do que grandes operações policiais.

“Está demonstrado que o caminho é ir na raiz do problema, é ir em quem são os financiadores do crime organizado, daqueles que fornecem as armas, que fornecem as drogas", pontuou Pantoja, que fez panfletagem em Bonsucesso, na Zona Norte do Rio.

A candidata citou a operação no Complexo da Maré, que deixou 12 feridos e um morto durante a manhã. 7 pessoas foram presas e milhares de crianças ficaram sem aulas nas unidades de ensino.

“Acontece das crianças ficarem com as aulas suspensas, como está acontecendo hoje na Maré. São 41 escolas que estão fechadas com as aulas suspensas, mais de 40 mil alunos que tiveram essas aulas suspensas, as pessoas que não podem sair para trabalhar e isso tudo enquanto não resolve o problema da segurança pública", declarou Pantoja, afirmando que é importante investir na justiça social para impedir que o crime organizado arregimente os moradores de comunidades.

“Nas favelas é necessário investir para garantir justiça social, é necessário que a gente tenha escola em tempo integral, tenha emprego, frentes emergenciais de trabalho para o nosso juventude, que inclusive é recrutada para o crime organizado, então é isso que nós da Unidade Popular queremos fazer", pontuou.

articles.title: Feiras livres em Aracaju: veja mudanças para as Eleições 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Pleito eleitoral altera programação das feiras realizadas da sexta-feira (2) a domingo (4).
articles.summary: As feiras livres em Aracaju serão antecipadas devido às Eleições 2026 e os mercados municipais fecharão no dia da votação; confira o novo cronograma.
articles.body:
Feira livre em Aracaju — Foto: PMA/Divulgação

A Prefeitura de Aracaju informou, nesta segunda-feira (28), que algumas feiras livres na capital sergipana terão os dias alterados por conta das Eleições 2026.

Com isso, as feiras realizadas tradicionalmente na sexta-feira serão antecipadas para quinta-feira, enquanto as de sábado acontecerão na sexta-feira e as de domingo serão realizadas no sábado. Os horários habituais permanecem os mesmos.

Confira a programação das feiras livres:

Na quinta-feira: São José, Suíssa, Castelo Branco, Médici, Sol Nascente, Agamenon Magalhães e Jessé Pinto Freire.

Na sexta-feira: Santo Antônio, 18 do Forte, Grageru, Cirurgia, São Carlos e Santa Tereza.

No sábado: Bugio, América, Santa Maria, Jardim Esperança e Dom Pedro.

A única exceção é a feira do Residencial Costa Nova, no Bairro Aruana, realizada na sexta-feira à tarde, que permanecerá no dia e horário tradicionais.

No dia do pleito, os mercados centrais Thales Ferraz, Antônio Franco e Maria Virgínia Franco, além dos mercados setoriais localizados nos bairros, estarão fechados. Os equipamentos reabrem na segunda-feira (5) em horário normal.

articles.title: How can the UK’s Labour Party rebuild voter trust?
articles.summary: Members at annual conference are optimistic about new PM
articles.body:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s leadership is being put to the test.

At their annual conference, members of the governing Labour Party seem hopeful he has solutions.

But Burnham is the United Kingdom’s seventh prime minister in the decade since it decided to leave the EU. And many voters have been moving to the right, particularly to support Reform UK.

Those are just some of the challenges standing in the way of the prime minister fulfilling his pledges.

articles.title: Cattle to feed: Why a global meat crisis is looming
articles.summary: World’s top three beef producers witness a decline in cattle stocks because of rising input costs, droughts and biology.
articles.body:
Beef prices are soaring in China. Across the Pacific Ocean in the United States, cattle farmers are complaining that their businesses are becoming increasingly unsustainable. And in India, poultry rearers are slashing their production targets because they cannot afford feed.

More than 90 percent of the world’s population eats meat in one form or another — and a looming meat crisis threatens to affect what they buy at the market, what they cook at home, and what’s served on the table.

At the heart of this is a chain of decisions and uncertainties that consumers rarely see. A cow has to be raised for years before it can become beef. Chickens need feed, much of it tied to global grain and soya bean markets. Farmers need land, water and weather conditions that allow them to keep animals alive and productive.

When any link in this chain is disrupted, a spiralling crisis ensues.

So what is putting the pressure on meat production, and what does it mean for billions of people around the world?

Declining cattle stocks in Brazil, US and China

Brazil, the US and China are the world’s three biggest beef producers, together supplying more than half of the world’s beef. But their cattle herds are shrinking at the same time.

According to a March estimate by the US Department of Agriculture (USDA), Brazil’s total herd this year is estimated at 177.4 million cattle — a nearly 8 percent drop from 192.5 million in 2024.

Over in the US, cattle numbers are at a historic low.

The USDA counted 86.2 million cattle and calves on farms on January 1, 2026. The number of beef cows — the females needed to produce future calves — was 27.6 million, down 1 percent from a year earlier. The 2025 calf crop was also down 2 percent.

In China, the USDA estimated a cattle head count of 94 million in January 2026, down 14 percent from 105 million in January 2024.

In all three cases, beef production is also projected to be down in 2026.

The USDA predicts a 2 percent decline in Brazil’s beef production and a 5 percent fall in exports. As for the US, beef production in 2026 is likely to be 4 percent lower than last year. China’s total beef supply this year is projected to be 12 percent lower than 2024.

The decline in domestic production, coupled with shrinking supplies that can be imported, has sent prices soaring in China — the world’s largest beef consumer and importer.

What’s driving down cattle herds and beef production?

The reasons are many, and they vary from country to country.

Brazil counts China and the European Union as two major markets for its beef exports. But both have imposed import restrictions that have disincentivised Brazilian beef manufacturers. That is partly responsible for the country’s decreased cattle head count, according to an analysis by Augusto Neto at S&P Global, the market intelligence firm.

Additionally, Brazil is currently in what is known as a cattle reversion cycle — when rearers reduce the slaughter of animals and instead try to preserve their female stock to help rebuild their herd — according to the USDA.

In the US, droughts have hit 60 percent of the country’s cattle-rearing area, according to a report by Sampad Nandy of S&P Global. With grazing areas decreasing, feed costs have risen.

Three major organisations, representing breeders in the states of Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas, issued a joint statement this week arguing that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raids were disrupting their already strained operations. The meat industry depends heavily on immigrant workers.

If beef prices are rising, shouldn’t rearers want to produce more beef?

In theory, yes. But in practice, high prices do not automatically mean that more cattle can be produced quickly.

Cattle production is constrained by biological supply cycles, Kenneth Foster, professor of agricultural economics at Purdue University, told Al Jazeera. It can take a couple of years for a producer who receives a signal from the market to expand production and actually see the resulting animals enter the beef supply. The quickest way to rebuild a herd is to keep female cattle that might otherwise have been sold and use them for breeding. That is what Brazil is now doing.

But that creates a difficult economic calculation. A producer can sell an animal today at a high price, or keep it for breeding and wait for the next generation. That means carrying the costs and risks of keeping the animal while waiting for it to reproduce.

The result is a market in which strong demand and limited supply can persist even when prices are already high.

The USDA expects the cattle herd to begin rebuilding in the US, but the process is gradual.

The US and Brazil cases illustrate one of the central problems facing meat production: sometimes the constraint is not technology, land or money.

Meanwhile, Europe presents a different picture. The continent is witnessing a structural change in what consumers are eating.

The EU produced about 42.7 million tonnes of meat in 2025. But EU meat production is projected to decline by about 3 percent between 2025 and 2035, with beef production projected to fall by 10 percent and pork by 7 percent. Poultry is the exception: production is projected to rise by 5 percent.

This shift is also visible in consumption.

Consumption of EU beef and pigmeat is projected to decline through 2035, while poultry consumption is expected to increase by 9 percent.

Beef and pork require longer production cycles and face different economic and environmental pressures. Poultry, by contrast, can respond much more quickly to changes in demand because chickens reach market weight within weeks rather than years.

That difference is becoming increasingly important. The OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook expects poultry to be the fastest-growing major meat category globally over the next decade, helped by its relatively low cost and short production cycle.

Europe is therefore becoming an example of how a meat system can adapt without simply producing more of everything. Some forms of meat become harder or more expensive to produce, while others expand to fill part of the space.

Poultry has problems too — as India shows

Yet the poultry industry faces its own challenges, with India offering an example.

In June, a large section of India’s poultry industry announced plans to cut production by 25 percent after soya meal prices rose by more than 40 percent in a month.

The decision was announced by the All India Poultry Breeders’ Association after producers faced sharply higher feed costs and a seasonal decline in demand. Producers also began culling parent breeder stocks — birds needed to produce future generations of poultry.

Soya meal is an important protein source in animal feed. When its price rises sharply, poultry producers face a choice: absorb higher costs, raise prices, or reduce the number of birds they produce.

In India’s case, producers chose to cut production.

The consequences extended beyond individual farms. The Reuters news agency reported in May that Indian soya meal prices had risen 41 percent in one month to a four-year high of 66,000 rupees ($687.5) per tonne. India subsequently cancelled 25,000 tonnes of soya meal export contracts and began turning to soya bean imports from African countries.

The takeaway: a shock in one part of the agricultural system can move quickly through the meat supply chain globally.

As farmers try to protect their livelihoods and families try to keep food on the table, changing climates, rising prices, shifting dietary preferences and growing trade barriers are together reshaping the future of meat — and what we eat.

articles.title: What have we learned about Pope Leo during his visit to France
articles.summary: France may have a highly secularized culture, but it has given Pope Leo XIV a superstar welcome.
articles.body: France may have a highly secularized culture, but it has given Pope Leo XIV a superstar welcome. In Paris, around 800,000 lined the Champs-Élysées avenue, some waving Vatican or French flags while others climbed trees or stood on each other’s shoulders to get a glimpse of the popemobile. In Lourdes, a holy site in southern France, around 150,000 attended an open-air papal Mass, according to Vatican estimates which dwarf the numbers of faithful who turned out for the last papal visit in 2008. During the four-day visit, Leo appeared comfortable and relaxed, delivering most of his speeches and reflections in French, as the Chicago-born pontiff sought to tackle several themes during the trip. A strong focus of Leo’s has been on trying to revitalize faith in a traditional European Catholic heartland as well as on addressing the clerical sexual abuse scandal and big political topics such as artificial intelligence. He’s also offered some more personal, unscripted remarks, helping to shape a clearer picture of himself. He wants Europe to draw on its Christian roots While his predecessor never made official visits to the major Catholic European countries of France and Spain, Pope Leo has traveled to both within the first year and a half since his election. France is sometimes described as the “eldest daughter of the church” because of its deep Catholic roots, but it’s also faced a long-term trend of declining church attendance with estimates of just 5-8% of the population heading to the pews each week. French bishops have more recently reported some good news though: a surprising rise in new church entrants after around 8,200 adolescents and 13,200 adults were baptized in 2026. That’s a 20% increase on the year prior, with the church also saying 42% of the adults seeking baptism are aged 18-25, a reflection of a trend showing Gen Z’s openness to religious faith. It’s something Pope Leo will have noted at the Stade de France when 80,000 young people packed the venue for a jubilant – and loud – prayer vigil. It was similar to when the pontiff visited Spain in June. “There is a quest for meaning. People need and are in search of meaning and answers to the big existential question,” Rev. Benoît Pouzin, a priest in southwest France involved in youth ministry, told CNN. France has a strict separation between church and state, so each papal visit needs to be carefully navigated. But in a surprising twist, Leo’s Mass in Paris was celebrated on the Place de la Concorde, a site deeply linked to the secular Republic as it’s where the last king of France, Louis XVI and Marie-Antoinette were guillotined. The separation of the church started with the fall of the monarchy during the French Revolution. In another unusual move later in the trip, President Emmanuel Macron also attended a papal Mass in Metz, a city in the northeast, despite criticism in 2023 for doing the same during Pope Francis’ visit. Pope isn’t panicking over AI, but warns of its power Many among the crowds also pointed to Leo’s role as the other major US leader on the world stage. It’s hard not to see him as a counterweight to President Donald Trump. In contrast to the Trump administration, the pope has called for stronger guardrails around the development of artificial intelligence, warning against a “paradise of machines” while in Paris. Pope Leo said he is taking the warnings about Artificial Intelligence’s threat to humanity seriously, and said it is irresponsible for people to sit back and dismiss the risks of AI. Trump has dismissed the warnings about AI as a “hoax” which he made during a surprise phone call with Jensen Huang, the CEO of chipmaker Nvidia, at a summit in Los Angeles. “I don’t think that that is fake news – as some have said – to try and pause,” Leo XIV said on board the papal plane from Metz to Rome. Leo, who has expressed a keen interest in artificial intelligence since the start of his papacy, said that he found it “interesting” that Huang had unveiled a new tool to prevent AI agents from operating out of human control. “He’s the same one, however, that says there should be no limits placed and no government regulation,” the Pope said. The pope devoted his first major theological document to AI earlier this year, warning about the use of AI in warfare and calling for stronger ethical foundation to the development of the technology. The pope explained that the Vatican had established its own AI commission to understand how to use it, along with the risks and benefits, and that “we need to continue to invite political leaders, the leaders of AI” so they can “look at what is happening already and what could be down the road.” He explained: “We are trying to continue to promote dialog, study, investigation, to find ways to make sure that AI does not get to a point where it could destroy humanity.” “If someone were to ask me, am I in panic mode? No, I’m not, I sleep at night” the pope said, but added: “I do think that the concerns raised by many of the experts, specialists in AI, should be taken seriously.” “To simply say, oh, it’s not going to happen and close our eyes to it, I think, is probably not the most responsible way to go about that,” Leo said. Concern over the far right and Christianity The pope, who spoke out against the US war in Iran, also wants a more united Europe, a stronger European Union and stronger international cooperation. “Today, relations between individuals and states are becoming increasingly uncivilized,” the pope said in Metz on Monday. “The value of keeping one’s word is dismissed; instead, people boast of lies and deceit.” The pope’s speech also praised one of the founders of the European Union, Robert Schuman, for whom there is an ongoing formal cause to make a saint. Pope Leo XIV has warned against the use of Christianity by far-right political groups, while calling on the church to be active in seeking to prevent extremism. Speaking on board the papal plane, he said that “the combination of these far-right points of view with a certain kind of religion” cannot be considered an “authentic expression of Christianity.” The pope’s comments came in response to a question about the rise of extremist parties in Germany as he flew back from making a major speech on European Unity at the French-German border. “We go back to the values of the Gospel [Christian teaching], which are not about hatred and division, but they’re about understanding and compassion,” the pope said. The American pontiff also responded to Trump’s White House media ban, which includes CNN and other outlets. In answer to a question from CNN, he said he was “very happy that, here, you are all welcome and good coverage, I think, is very important and that we have it all the way around, for everyone.” The response was classic Leo: signaling his support for the press but not wishing to create an unnecessary dispute with the president. The American pope’s in-flight interactions with journalists were rare, unscripted moments, with his answers often revealing more about his personality. On the flight from Rome to Paris, the pope was asked if he had anything to do with a miraculous recent Chicago White Sox victory, his beloved baseball team. “No comment,” he said before adding with a smile, “Great things happen in Chicago.” He also recalled childhood memories of watching Fulton Sheen, the American archbishop and broadcaster who was recently declared “blessed,” one step ahead of sainthood, and revealed he’d been practicing his French but was no longer using the Duolingo language app. “It’s fake news!” he said about recent reports. Leo has in the past been spotted using Duolingo to learn German. Leo isn’t simply vocal about challenges of his homeland. He also voiced concern over assisted dying with France recently approving legislation granting the right to the incurably ill, which is strongly opposed by the Catholic Church. Leo spoke on the subject several times during his visit – most clearly in the “miracle shrine” town of Lourdes, known for drawing many sick and terminally ill pilgrims to its shrine. A willingness to tackle church scandal The pope must, however, continue to wrestle with Catholic Church’s sexual abuse scandals. France was left shocked by a 2021 report that estimated around 330,000 children were sexually abused over 70 years by priests or other church figures. He addressed this by telling crowds the church must admit its own failings and heal “deep wounds” before holding a two-hour meeting with seven survivors of abuse. The Vatican said that Leo thanked them “for their painful testimony” while “reaffirming his commitment to ensuring that the harm they suffered is not repeated for others.” But the scandal still lingers. On the façade of the basilica in Lourdes, banners were placed over controversial mosaics ahead of Leo’s visit. These mosaics – which will now be covered indefinitely – were designed by a Slovenian priest and artist, Rev. Marko Rupnik, accused of sexual and psychological abuse of adult women. A local bishop said the pope backed how the apostolic nunciature was handling the artist’s works. Bishop Jean-Marc Micas also said Leo had ordered the Vatican’s in-house media outlets to stop using Rupnik art. Rupnik, who maintains his innocence, is facing a church trial in the Vatican, which complainants say is taking too long and lacks transparency. The pope was elected 16-months ago and is still carving out a narrative for his papacy. Some in the Vatican find him difficult to read, and the pope is known for keeping his cards close to his chest. But it’s out on the open road when he travels abroad, in France and, in November, in Latin America, where the Leo papacy is beginning to take shape.

articles.title: Netanyahu should be held accountable for failing to stop Oct. 7
articles.summary: Marine veteran Joslin Joseph argues that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu must be held accountable for failing to act on multiple warnings prior to the Oct. 7 attacks.
articles.body:
In the aftermath of 9/11, Americans started asking hard questions to our politicians. How could they not see this coming? Did they have an inkling that something was about to happen? What did our intelligence communities miss? It became obvious that the FBI was tracking several of the hijackers in this country, and it was well known that Osama bin Laden had been on the CIA’s radar for some time. But a lack of communication combined with the refusal to take these threats seriously led to an environment where these attacks did happen.

It was a lesson that Americans and people around the world learned, as they all have had to deal with terrorism, both domestic and international within their own borders. It could be said that it wasn’t the U.S. that led the way, but Israel who had a long track record of foiling terror plots against Israelis both at home and abroad. It made the attacks on Oct. 7 all the more shocking.

We are coming up on the third anniversary of Oct. 7, and we just had Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu come to our country and talk down to us . And by us, I mean all of his critics from the mayor of New York City to ordinary Americans frustrated with the perceived influence of Israel on American foreign policy. It seems that Netanyahu is just trying to distract from his own failures to protect his own people.

In the aftermath of the attacks, I was sent a video of Charlie Kirk. Now, I am nowhere near Kirk politically speaking, but this particular video was intriguing to me. Like Kirk, I had visited the Holy Land on a pilgrimage with my parents. Being a Marine vet, in addition to taking in the holy sites and tourist spots, I noticed the incredible military and police presence in the area. On a trip to Bethlehem to visit the birthplace of Jesus Christ, we had to switch from an Israeli tour guide to a Palestinian. We struck up a conversation and I asked what it was like living with the Israelis. We talked about his lack of rights, the checkpoints, how hard it was to work, and the constant surveillance of the Israelis after the Second Intifada. But he told me, this was nothing compared to how Gaza was. He said something I would later hear from Kirk’s own mouth: Gaza was the most surveilled place in the world .

CNN took Hamas propaganda videos of their training for the attacks and showed us (in October 2023) how the terrorist group trained not in a foreign country like Iran or Afghanistan, but in Gaza . And they weren’t hiding in tunnels. They were training out in the open for all to see, using real guns and explosives. They conducted military exercises less than a half mile from the border checkpoint they would later overrun, in broad daylight. There was no way that the Israelis did not know an attack was coming.

There are reports that Netanyahu was warned about the attacks and did nothing . The BBC among others reported a mere five days after the attack that the Egyptians had sent a warning to Netanyahu in advance. We now know that warning came over a week before the attack happened . If that wasn’t bad enough, Haaretz, an Israeli-based news organization broke that the United Arab Emirates also warned Netanyahu of the attack in September of 2023.

Now, I can’t and won’t speak into what Netanyahu was thinking or what he thought was going to happen. But I do know that he was facing a lot of trouble with charges of corruption and massive demonstrations against his efforts to remake Israel’s Supreme Court. He also took power making promises to hard-line factions that have a very sinister view toward all Palestinians.

It is baffling that Netanyahu was never held accountable for his failures to protect his own people. I get that there was a need to get the hostages back and a change in leadership might have been bad. But there still should have been some accountability, especially from the American end. Sending money and arms to Israel has grown more unpopular on both sides of the aisle. Many people think the current war in Iran was at the behest of Netanyahu and his PowerPoint presentation to President Trump in the White House Situation Room.

The time for accountability is now, and better late than never. His knowledge and lack of action on the warnings (both internal and external) put the Israelis in such a bad position militarily that the attacks were worse than they should have been. It is not certain that the Oct. 7 attacks could have been prevented, but surely their magnitude could have been mitigated with preventive actions.

Netanyahu will soon face a general election . Now is as good a time as any to finally hold him accountable for his failure to protect his own people.

Joslin Joseph is a recipient of the Military Reporters and Editors award for Best Commentary-Opinion. A graduate of Harvard and Ohio State, he is a Marine veteran who served in Iraq. He currently lives in Anaheim, Calif.

articles.title: Ben-Gvir joins hundreds of Israelis to storm Al-Aqsa Mosque compound
articles.summary: Israeli national security minister declares ‘we are the owners of the place in Al-Aqsa’ amid heavily guarded incursion.
articles.body:
Hundreds of Israelis led by far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir have stormed the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound under police protection.

The Jerusalem governorate on Monday said Israeli forces closed intersections and streets surrounding the Old City that lead to the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound, which Jews refer to as the Temple Mount, in occupied East Jerusalem on the third day of the Jewish holiday of Sukkot.

It said the Israelis danced in circles and sang inside the courtyards of Al-Aqsa Mosque during the raid, noting that 900 people entered the compound in the morning.

“We are the owners of the place in Al-Aqsa and in the prisons, and we have turned the lives of terrorist prisoners into hell,” Ben-Gvir said.

“The people of Israel are on the path to absolute victory, and today we pray in Al-Aqsa, which is the most important place for the Jewish people.”

Monday’s intrusion came as Israeli authorities forced dozens of Palestinian shopkeepers to close their businesses and residents to remain inside their homes in areas near the mosque to allow Jewish prayers during Sukkot.

“Dozens of Palestinian owners of shops, cafes and restaurants in the Cotton Merchants Market in Jerusalem’s Old City were forced to close them during the Jewish Sukkot holiday to make way for Jewish prayers in the market,” the Association for Civil Rights in Israel said in a statement.

Palestinian presidential spokesman Nabil Abu Rudeineh described the incursion as “playing with fire and a dangerous provocation to the feelings of Muslims around the world”.

He also warned that Israel was seeking to ignite a “religious war” in the region.

Since 2003, Israeli police have allowed groups of Israelis to make daily incursions into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound, except on Fridays and Saturdays.

Israel often imposes restrictions on Palestinian worshippers. It prevented Eid al-Fitr prayers at Al-Aqsa this year, allowing only 10,000 Palestinians from the occupied West Bank, home to 3.3 million people, into one of Islam’s holiest sites for the first Friday prayers of Ramadan.

articles.title: Scottish crime writer Peter May dies aged 74
articles.summary: May was one of Scotland's most prolific television and crime writers and sold 15 million books around the world.
articles.body:
Peter May, one of Scotland's most prolific television writers and crime authors, has died at the age of 74.

The news of his death was announced by his wife and fellow author Janice Hally, who said she had "no words" to express the loss.

May died on Friday at his home in the south of France where he had lived for many years and had been nominated for several awards.

He sold about 15 million copies of his books around the world, and the novel he said would be his last - Island of the Dead - is to be published in January 2027.

A tribute from close friend and publisher, Jon Riley, said although May had announced his retirement and was looking forward to sharing it with his beloved wife, he found there was one more novel in him.

Riley said May was preparing for a farewell tour of Scotland and Lewis to coincide with publication of his last novel in January.

He went onto say May was not only one of the best writers of crime fiction but he inspired "enormous affection" in his readers and those who worked with him.

He said: "His kindness, generosity and largeness of spirit, loyalty, engagement with life, and the world, made him a much-loved, as well as much- admired figure.

Born in Glasgow, May began his career as a journalist in Scotland, winning Young Journalist of the Year at age 21, and published his first novel, The Reporter, at the age of 26 in 1976.

After it was adapted as a BBC drama series, he quit journalism for television, and became a successful scriptwriter and producer on Take the High Road and the Gaelic soap Machair, set on the Isle of Lewis.

The first book in May's 'Lewis Trilogy', The Blackhouse, was first published in French in 2009 and then in English in 2011. It won the 2011 Cezam Prix Littéraire Inter CE - a readers' prize for best novel by a European author, published in France.

First Minister John Swinney expressed his regret at hearing news of May's death.

He said: "I have hugely enjoyed Peter May's evocative books set in the Hebrides.

"His description of events in some of the most precious places in our landscape was so stunning.

articles.title: Giant pandas arrive in Atlanta after Trump-Xi meeting
articles.summary: Two giant pandas touched down in Atlanta on Sunday, three days after Chinese President Xi Jinping announced their impending arrival. The pandas, male Ping Ping and female Fu Shuang, arrived at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, according to Zoo Atlanta. The bears arrived via a FedEx-donated Boeing 777 aircraft that features a panda eating bamboo painted…
articles.body:
Two giant pandas touched down in Atlanta on Sunday, three days after Chinese President Xi Jinping announced their impending arrival .

The pandas, male Ping Ping and female Fu Shuang, arrived at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, according to Zoo Atlanta . The bears arrived via a FedEx-donated Boeing 777 aircraft that features a panda eating bamboo painted near the front of the fuselage.

Ping Ping and Fu Shuang were born at the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding in 2020. They are not yet visible and will be quarantined for roughly a month, the zoo noted.

Raymond King, the president and CEO of Zoo Atlanta, said the pandas’ arrival marked a “thrilling day” for the zoo and a “historic moment” for the city and Georgia.

“We are elated to welcome Ping Ping and Fu Shuang and could not be more excited about sharing that joy with our Members, guests, city, and community in the coming weeks,” King said in a release.

“Zoo Atlanta is honored to partner with the China Wildlife Conservation Association to see important work continue toward the conservation of giant pandas, which is the most important benefit of guarding this species,” he added.

During a White House meeting with President Trump on Thursday, Xi announced the two pandas would soon arrive in the Peach State.

“The giant panda has been an envoy of friendship between the Chinese and the Americans,” the Chinese leader remarked in the Oval Office.

“Here, I have a piece of good news. In a few days, two pandas — Ping Ping and Fu Shuang — will come to their new home in Zoo Atlanta and meet with the American people,” Xi added.

Panda diplomacy between China and the U.S. is not new. After former President Nixon visited the Asian country in 1972, the Chinese government sent giant pandas Ling Ling and Hsing Hsing to the National Zoo in Washington, D.C.

Through cooperation between the China Wildlife Conservation Association and multiple American zoos, pandas have bred and raised 17 cubs over the past three decades in Atlanta, San Diego and Washington, according to Chinese state media .

The International Union for Conservation of Nature moved giant pandas from “endangered” to “vulnerable” last year. The giant panda population increased by 17 percent over the last decade, per the World Wildlife Fund .

articles.title: Congo Ebola outbreak tops 8,000 cases as health worker shortages worsen
articles.summary: The number of confirmed cases of Ebola virus in Congo has surged past 8,000, as the country runs out of health workers to contain the deadly disease.
articles.body: The number of confirmed cases of Ebola virus in Congo has surged past 8,000, as the country runs out of health workers to contain the deadly disease. Congo announced an outbreak on May 15, caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, which has no known treatment or vaccine, and has struggled to contain it. The latest data from Congo’s health ministry released Sunday showed that 8,067 cases have been confirmed, with 3,901 deaths as of Sept. 26 across 63 health zones in seven of the country’s 26 provinces, with a fatality rate of more than 48%. “The continuously high crude case fatality ratio, and especially the continuously high rate of deaths occurring in communities, highlights the seriousness of the disease and the persistent challenges in timely case detection and access to early and adequate patient care,” the World Health Organization said in its latest report. It means that a large percentage of those infected were dying, without taking into account factors like delay in seeking help and response, or hidden cases. Last week, WHO said that Congo was running out of health workers to contain the disease. Health workers have complained about delayed or missing payments, triggering several strikes. According to the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 50 health workers have died since the outbreak was announced. Some areas have shown signs of improvement, with fewer confirmed cases in the past several weeks, including in Ituri province and Haut-Uele, but officials say the disease is spreading further in other areas, expanding its geographical reach. According to data from the Africa CDC, the current outbreak has outpaced the two-year West Africa regional outbreak in terms of spread in the same time. By week 19, the regional outbreak between 2014 and 2016 recorded 3,781 cases, while the current outbreak recorded 7,840. WHO said that it’s on track to surpass the regional outbreak, which killed 11,000 people. Containment efforts have been hamstrung by insecurity, displacement, a health workers’ strike and intense population movements.

articles.title: I had independence, routine, and a sense that I was moving forward: Ex-NRI shares struggle adjusting in India after spending years in US
articles.summary: A Redditor who came back to India six months ago after spending years in the US shared the feeling of loneliness in India, even though he moved closer to
articles.body: A Redditor who came back to India six months ago after spending years in the US shared the feeling of loneliness in India, even though he moved closer to his family and the relocation was also because of his family. While many such Reddit posts deal with job scenarios, weather, pollution, traffic and infrastructure issues in India and the US, this post went viral as it resonated with many who find it difficult after coming back to India -- for no particular reason."I’ve been back in India for about 6 months after spending a significant amount of time in the US, and honestly, I’m struggling more than I expected. I came back mainly because my parents were worried about me, and I also wanted to be closer to home and take care of myself. At the time, coming back felt like the right thing to do. But now I feel incredibly lonely," the post said.The Redditor said old friends are busy with their own lives and don't make an effort to meet. "I don’t really have friends here anymore. My old friends have their own lives now, and everyone seems busy. I’ve tried initiating plans and reaching out, but nobody has really made the effort to meet. I understand that people are busy and that life changes, but after repeatedly trying, it starts to feel like I’m the only one who cares about maintaining these friendships," the post added."Even my relationship with my brother feels different now. I thought coming home would make me feel closer to my family, but somehow I feel more disconnected than I expected," it said.In contrast, the Redditor said that his life in the US has a routine, independence, peopl around him and a sense that he was moving forward."I know I can’t go back and change the decision, and I don’t want to blame my parents either. They were genuinely worried about me and wanted me home. But emotionally, this transition has been much harder than I imagined," the person wrote.The comment section was divided as many said that six months is too little a time to readjust while many said that NRIs should not expect that India would stand still when they come back after years

articles.title: Iran denies link to attack on airbase as UK minister warns of ‘proxies’
articles.summary: Tehran condemns ‘unfounded and malicious speculation’; British FM vows to ‘act against the proxies of Iran’.
articles.body:
Iran has denied any involvement in a suspected plot targeting the Fairford Airbase in the United Kingdom.

Iran’s embassy in London condemned in a statement on Monday the “fabricated speculations” linking Tehran to the incident. Five British nationals were arrested in the vicinity of the base, which hosts United States military aircraft that have been used to bomb Iran amid the conflict between the two countries.

The suspects were detained on Sunday morning on suspicion of the “preparation of a terrorist act”. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said on Monday that the UK must be prepared to “confront” all security threats facing Europe and the world, adding: “We will act against the proxies of Iran.”

Iran’s embassy in London said that it “categorically rejects and strongly condemns the recent unfounded and malicious speculations published by some British individuals and media outlets”, asserting that the accusations would fuel “Iranophobia propaganda” in Britain.

Iran reserves the right to “take appropriate legal measures”, it added.

British police have not thus far linked Iran to the arrests as Counter Terrorism Policing continues investigating.

British security officials are exploring “multiple lines of enquiry” on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act and “preparation of a terrorist act”.

The UK government gave the US authorisation to use bombers based at the RAF Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

On Sunday, a source familiar with the investigation said an Iranian-linked motive is considered the most likely, while a Russian sabotage operation or an Islamist plot were also being looked at.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) had said in July that the Fairford base was a legitimate target.

British police arrested the five men after receiving a tip that three suspicious vehicles appeared to be heading towards the base in southwest England.

In their statement on Monday, the counterterrorism police identified the men as British nationals aged 23 to 25 from London.

On Monday afternoon, the head of UK Counter Terrorism Policing said the five were being released on bail “following extensive interviews and inquiries”.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor added: “To be very clear, this does not mean that the investigation is over. They are subject to stringent conditions on their movement and contact with others”.

US President Donald Trump said the suspects had been looking to ‌do “big damage” and had been under investigation by British and US authorities “for a long time, and we got them”.

Following news of their release, the US leader, who said the case “might be” linked to Iran, told reporters: “I’m surprised that they released them, I wouldn’t have done that.”

⁠UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham ⁠was due on Monday to chair a meeting of the COBRA emergency ‌response team as British authorities continue to investigate the incident.

articles.title: DHS tears into MS NOW after host touts ‘anti-authoritarian’ ICE monitoring group
articles.summary: DHS slammed MS NOW for featuring activists who train 'ICE Watch' volunteers and are now turning their organizing efforts toward the midterm elections.
articles.body: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) fired back at MS NOW on Sunday after "Connect with Jacob Soboroff" host Jacob Soboroff highlighted an activist group that trains "ICE Watch" volunteers to monitor federal immigration operations and is now turning some of that organizing toward the midterm elections. During Saturday's edition of the show, Soboroff discussed reporting about activists who previously monitored U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations and are now turning their attention toward election-related activity. MS NOW's description of the episode said, "ICE watchers once alerted neighbors about the presence of federal agents, now they are protecting the polls." Soboroff’s segment featured Zachary Mueller, a senior strategist for the nonprofit, States at the Core, and referenced reporting from the outlet "The Intercept" about activists preparing to monitor polling locations. States at the Core has described its work as opposing what it views as authoritarianism and has advertised trainings on both ICE monitoring and election protection. NEW YORK TIMES TORCHED FOR ‘FALSE’ REPORTING ON ICE INVESTIGATIONS, OUTLET FIRES BACK DHS pointed to attacks and threats against immigration officers while arguing that tools used to track federal agents could endanger law enforcement personnel and interfere with operations. "Shame on MS NOW for promoting efforts to undermine those who keep our communities and streets safe from illegal alien crime," a DHS spokesperson said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "ICE tracking apps put the lives of the men and women of law enforcement in danger as they go after terrorists, vicious gangs and violent criminal rings. "Our law officers are facing an over 1,600% increase in assaults, a 3,300% increase in vehicle attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats. Further, these apps are a method to interfere with law enforcement activities and harbor illegal aliens." States at the Core said in March that tens of thousands of Americans had attended its ICE Watch training before it launched a program called "Beyond ICE Watch," which sought to expand neighborhood organizing beyond monitoring immigration enforcement. SEVEN NONCITIZENS CHARGED IN NORTH TEXAS ELECTION-INTEGRITY INVESTIGATION The organization described its mission in that announcement. "Our mission is pretty simple. Help everyday people fight authoritarianism; help people fight for their freedoms," States at the Core said. In September, the group advertised a training that sought to adapt ICE Watch techniques for the midterm elections, including documenting activity around communities and elections. DHS SECRETARY BASHES NEW YORK LEADERSHIP AFTER ANNOUNCING THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS IN SWEEPING OPERATION States at the Core had previously drawn scrutiny for its ICE-monitoring tactics. In February, co-founder Jill Garvey trained "rapid responders" to use the military-derived "SALUTE" observation method — an acronym for size, activity, location, uniform, time and equipment — when documenting federal immigration personnel. The FBI was also investigating alleged Signal groups used by anti-ICE activists to track, identify and potentially impede federal law enforcement officers. FBI Director Kash Patel said investigations would examine whether the alleged coordination crossed the line into violations of federal law. DHS has reported a sharp increase in assaults against ICE personnel. The department said 647 assaults occurred between Jan. 20, 2025, and Sept. 20, 2026, compared with 37 during the corresponding period under the Biden administration, representing a 1,649% increase. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE DHS told Fox News Digital that it viewed messaging that encourages resistance to immigration enforcement as dangerous. "Glorifying resistance to lawful immigration enforcement is irresponsible and dismissive of the victims and families who have suffered because of crimes committed by criminal illegal aliens," the spokesperson said. "Assaulting and obstructing ICE law enforcement is a crime and felony. Anyone who assaults law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law." articles.title: UK pledges tougher stance on Israeli actions in Gaza, West Bank
articles.summary: British foreign minister vows to ‘match word with action’ when it comes to defending Palestinian rights.
articles.body:
The United Kingdom’s government is set to take a tougher stance on Israel’s actions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, the foreign minister has stated.

Addressing the Labour Party conference, Foreign Minister Ed Miliband called the Israeli government’s actions in the Palestinian territories “a stain on the conscience of the world”, and pledged new sanctions.

“I want to say to the millions of people in this country, and indeed elsewhere, who have been moved and outraged by the plight of the Palestinian people, ‘We hear you. You were right.'” Miliband said.

“We call out ethnic cleansing by the settler terrorists in the West Bank. We call out the evidence of war crimes in Gaza. We call out Israel’s illegal occupation of Palestine, and we match word with action,” he added before listing measures targeting economic links with Israeli settlements.

These included banning the import of goods from illegal settlements and disrupting the supply lines for British finance, British construction, and British services towards illegal settlements.

Miliband said that the ruling party has “reset its approach” under the leadership of Prime Minister Andy Burnham .

However, the government has been criticised for continued links to the Israeli government and for its treatment of pro-Palestinian protesters.

Dozens were arrested outside the conference in the northwestern city of Liverpool as they rallied in support of the banned Palestine Action group.

Miliband, who is Jewish, also warned against efforts to undermine the prospect of a Palestinian state, saying Labour would oppose moves that threaten the two-state solution.

Britain and other countries have voiced particular concern about the approval by Israel of the E1 settlement project east of Jerusalem, which would effectively cut the occupied West Bank in two.

Earlier this month, the UK government announced a ban on the import of all goods produced by illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the country’s most significant policy since London’s historic recognition of Palestinian statehood last year.

Burnham said that by enacting the ban, Britain was being true to its roots and taking a stand for “fairness against injustice”.

Miliband said when the ban was announced that “settler terrorists” were carrying out “ethnic cleansing” of Palestinians, adding that there had been “houses bulldozed, roads and public infrastructure destroyed, families displaced from their homes”.

Miliband added that he feels “a deep sense of shame about what has unfolded in Palestine under the eyes of the international community”.

articles.title: Nigeria's Ben Dancer attempts to break world record for non-stop dancing
articles.summary: Crowds have gathered in Lagos to watch Ben Dancer, who says he will carry on dancing until Tuesday morning.
articles.body:
A Nigerian dancer is attempting to dance non-stop for seven days in order to set a new world record.

Benjamin Daniel, known as Ben Dancer, is aiming to dance for 168 hours - 41 hours longer than the current record for the longest individual dance marathon.

Guinness World Records has yet to confirm whether the attempt qualifies as an official record. The BBC has contacted the organisation for comment.

Young people have been gathering in recent days to cheer him on at Freedom Park in Lagos, filming his every move and dancing along from behind the barriers.

"It's a beautiful moment. Seeing how far he has come and witnessing him achieve this feat made me incredibly proud and grateful to God," Uche Anumudu, one of those watching, told the BBC.

The current record is 127 hours, set by Indian dancer Srushti Sudhir Jagtap in 2023, when she was 16. Her performance focused mainly on kathak, one of India's major classical dance forms.

Ben Dancer, 33, has been dancing professionally for 18 years.

His attempt began on Tuesday 22 September and, if he completes the planned 168 hours, he is due to reach his target early on Tuesday morning.

For much of the marathon, Ben Dancer has drawn on Nigeria's rich dance traditions as well as its fast-changing internet culture.

Afrobeats has been a constant presence, alongside genres including fuji, jazz and zouk.

At times, he has swapped his dance clothes for traditional Nigerian outfits, including the flowing agbada and dashiki.

Nigeria has more than 250 ethnic groups, with a wide range of cultural traditions.

Ben Dancer's team says the performance is intended to reflect that diversity, rather than simply test his physical endurance.

His team says he underwent intensive fitness training before the attempt, changing his diet and focusing on carbohydrates and cardiovascular conditioning.

During the marathon, he has been eating lightly and drinking fluids while taking the permitted five minutes of rest for every continuous hour of activity.

Ben Dancer has chosen to dance for several hours at a time before taking his accumulated rest.

A medical team has also been present at Freedom Park to provide assistance when needed.

The scene around him has become something of a street party. Crowds of young people have gathered to cheer him on.

Videos from the attempt have gone viral across social media platforms, drawing more people to the venue.

Moronumubo Akodu, who has repeatedly visited to support Ben Dancer, said she was impressed by his determination but worried about the physical toll.

"It is actually insane but I am so proud of him," she told the BBC.

Emmanuel Ulelu, who visited the performance twice, said he noticed a striking change in the dancer's energy.

"On day two, you could see the stress," he said.

"Even after just three hours of dancing at the location myself, I wondered how he would keep going."

But when he returned 16 hours into day five, he said Ben Dancer appeared more energetic than before.

"It reminded me that we're capable of doing unbelievable things when how badly we want something matches and surpasses the difficulty of achieving it," he said.

Nigeria has also developed a strong relationship with Guinness World Records, particularly in entertainment.

In 2023, Nigerian chef Hilda Baci cooked continuously for 93 hours and 11 minutes in Lagos, which Guinness officially recognised as a new record.

Her achievement sparked a surge of interest in record attempts in Nigeria, even though others have since surpassed her.

Guinness says it received more than 1,500 new applications from the country within two months of her cook-a-thon, including events such as reading, singing, and crocheting.
